comments.note: The defence-in-depth path.resolve() check on lines 1302-1305 uses `filePath.startsWith(dialoguesDir + '/')` — on macOS /tmp is a symlink to /private/tmp. resolve() normalises this correctly so the check works, but a test on a symlinked root could expose subtle mismatches. Low risk given tests use real temp directories and all pass.

The DIALOGUE_FILENAME_RE allowlist /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.md$/ correctly rejects all path traversal patterns. The defence-in-depth resolve() prefix check provides a second layer. Security posture is solid.

summary: Reviewed 3 files: mcp-server/gui/api.ts (handleListDialogues + handleGetDialogueFile additions at lines ~1220–1323), mcp-server/gui/server.ts (route registrations), mcp-server/tests/gui/api.test.ts (11 new tests). Full OWASP Top 10 review performed. 0 Critical, 0 High findings. 2 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info finding — none blocking. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: OWASP A01 — Broken Access Control: No authentication or authorisation layer on any API route, including the new dialogues endpoints. This is a pre-existing design choice — the server is documented as a localhost-only developer tool (port 3420, no public exposure intended). The corsHeaders() helper restricts the CORS Allow-Origin to http://localhost:<port>, which is an appropriate restriction for the intended deployment model. The new endpoints inherit the same access-control posture as all other routes. No regression introduced. Risk is acceptable given local-only deployment.

OWASP A01 — Broken Access Control: In server.ts line 280, the filename path segment is decoded with decodeURIComponent() before passing to handleGetDialogueFile(). A client can percent-encode path-traversal characters (e.g. '%2E%2E%2Fsecret.md' → '../secret.md'). This is the correct approach — decoding before the allowlist check ensures DIALOGUE_FILENAME_RE at api.ts line 1295 sees the canonical form and correctly rejects the traversal. Verified: the decoded value '../secret.md' fails /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.md$/ and is rejected. No bypass is possible. Noted for completeness; no action needed.

OWASP A03 — Injection / OWASP A01 — Input Validation: The ?wp= query parameter (wpId) in handleListDialogues (api.ts lines 1261–1263) is used as a string prefix filter on in-memory filenames from readdir(). It is NOT used as part of any filesystem path — the path is constructed solely from the validated slug and the static 'dialogues' constant. There is no injection risk. However, wpId is accepted without validation: any arbitrary string is accepted (e.g. '../../../../etc', 'A'.repeat(10000)). The prefix filter is purely cosmetic (if no filenames start with that prefix, an empty array is returned), so there is no security impact. A low-risk improvement would be validating wpId against /^WP-[0-9]+$/ to enforce expected format and prevent log noise from malformed inputs.

OWASP A05 — Security Misconfiguration: The server does not set security-related HTTP response headers (Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy). This is a pre-existing gap affecting all routes, not introduced by WP-015. For a localhost developer tool this is low risk. The new dialogue routes inherit this gap identically. Recommended as a future hardening task rather than a blocker.

OWASP A09 — Security Logging & Monitoring: The new dialogue handlers do not log access attempts (successful or failed). Specifically, rejected traversal attempts in handleGetDialogueFile() are silently returned as 404 with no server-side log entry. For a localhost tool this is acceptable, but recording a stderr warning on DIALOGUE_FILENAME_RE rejection would aid debugging without leaking sensitive data. No action required for sign-off.

A02/A08 — No new dependencies introduced by this WP. The implementation uses only Node.js built-ins (node:fs/promises, node:path) already present in the codebase. No CVE scan needed. No supply-chain risk from this change.

Defence-in-depth assessment: Two independent path-traversal controls are applied in handleGetDialogueFile(). Primary: DIALOGUE_FILENAME_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.md$/ (api.ts line 1225) rejects anything containing '.', '/', or other special characters — this alone is sufficient to block all traversal. Secondary: path.resolve() prefix check (lines 1302–1305) ensures the resolved file path stays inside the dialoguesDir. Both layers are correctly implemented. The regex also correctly anchors start (^) and end ($), preventing partial matches.

Reviewed mcp-server/gui/api.ts (handleListDialogues lines 1237–1267, handleGetDialogueFile lines 1287–1315, isNodeError helper lines 1321–1323, DIALOGUE_FILENAME_RE constant line 1225), mcp-server/gui/server.ts (route registrations lines 270–310), and mcp-server/tests/gui/api.test.ts (handleListDialogues + handleGetDialogueFile suites, lines 1241–1358). All 10 ACs confirmed against source. Implementation is well-structured, security controls are correctly layered (DIALOGUE_FILENAME_RE primary allowlist + resolve() prefix secondary), route dispatch ordering is correct (4-segment dialogues route correctly precedes generic work-packages/:wpId), and test coverage is comprehensive with 11 new real-filesystem tests covering all traversal and edge cases.

comments.note: Route dispatch ordering in server.ts is correct: the 4-segment '/api/projects/:slug/dialogues/:filename' branch (lines 270–282) is placed BEFORE the generic '/api/projects/:slug/work-packages/:wpId' branch (lines 284–294). Both match rest.length===4; without this ordering, dialogue file requests would be misrouted to the work-packages handler. The inline comment on line 271 documents this intentionally, which is good practice.

isNodeError() helper (api.ts line 1321–1323) is correctly scoped as module-private (no export). The `err instanceof Error && 'code' in err` check is the idiomatic TypeScript pattern for Node.js ErrnoException detection. Placed after the function that uses it; hoisting is not required since it is a function declaration at module scope. Clean.

Security auditor observation confirmed: the ?wp= wpId parameter is a pure in-memory prefix filter and never touches the filesystem. No injection risk. The low-priority suggestion to validate it against /^WP-[0-9]+$/ is noted but is not a blocker — returning an empty array for unmatched filters is safe and correct behavior.

No observations — code is clean and consistent. handleListDialogues and handleGetDialogueFile are clearly documented with JSDoc, parameter semantics are explicit, and error paths are covered. The isNodeError helper avoids the `as NodeJS.ErrnoException` cast anti-pattern. Implementation matches the codebase's existing style conventions.
